about: By hand: the terms a search names an article or a law by when no source does: a term of the law or of its practice (wanprestatie), an English word (GDPR, minimum wage) or an abbreviation the sources do not give. Each term has its variants, the one article (`law`: a BWB id or CELEX number, `article`: its number as the graph has it; without one the law itself) it is about, and `why`: the source that ties them. A term is added only after its article has been read: it exists, holds and rules the term. A law abbreviation the sources give (Awb, Sr, AVG) needs no entry. A term or variant is one concept's only, compared in lower case without accents and punctuation. `lawgraph curated set concepts`.
